finding.claim: transfer_funds calls check_csrf() (which only returns a boolean) and ignores the result, so the CSRF check is never enforced. A cross-site forged POST from a victim's browser transfers funds from the victim's account to an attacker-chosen account.
finding.source: Attacker-hosted page auto-submitting a cross-site POST with amt and to fields; the victim has a logged-in session cookie
finding.sink: UPDATE acct SET bal = bal - ? / bal + ? at lines 17-18

trace.note: check_csrf returns bool, does not exit

finding.guards_checked: verify_csrf (which enforces) is used in update_profile but not here; no SameSite or Origin check visible in this file; session_start only

verdict.guard_found: check_csrf (actions.php:4-6) returns a bool; its result is discarded at line 16. verify_csrf (the enforcing variant) is only used in update_profile. No auth check, SameSite setting or Origin check exists in the file; session_start only.
verdict.reason: actions.php:16 calls check_csrf() as a bare statement, so the boolean from line 5 is ignored and the UPDATEs at lines 17-18 run for any cross-site POST carrying the victim's session cookie (verify_csrf at lines 9-12 would exit, but is not called here).

finding.claim: The transfer amount is not validated: a negative amt makes the debit add to the caller's balance and subtract from the recipient, so the caller can drain any account id given in 'to'. There is also no balance check, so overdraft is allowed. The two updates are not in a transaction and 'to' is not checked to exist, so money can vanish.
finding.source: Authenticated user's POST amt (e.g. -1000000) and to (victim account id)
finding.sink: UPDATE acct SET bal = bal - ? / bal + ? at lines 17-18

trace.note: bal = bal - (-N) increases the attacker's balance

finding.guards_checked: No sign, range or numeric check; no balance >= amt condition in the WHERE clause; no transaction or lock; no check that the user is authenticated or that uid is set

verdict.guard_found: Only check_csrf() at actions.php:16, whose bool result is discarded (the verify_csrf variant is used only in update_profile). Even if it were enforced, it only blocks CSRF and not a user submitting their own request. There is no amount validation, balance check, transaction, or existence check on 'to'.
verdict.reason: actions.php:17-18 pass the unvalidated $_POST['amt'] straight into bal - ? and bal + ?, so a negative amt moves money from the account in 'to' to the caller. The only control, check_csrf at actions.php:16, is a bare statement whose result is ignored and does not touch amount logic.
